item: IT strategy explicitly mapped to business goals, reviewed at least twice a year
Clear ownership of technology roadmap (cloud, data platforms, ERP/CRM, AI tooling)
Board/exec reporting on IT value delivery, not just uptime metrics
Vendor and platform consolidation reviewed to cut redundant spend
Formal AI adoption strategy (not just pilots) with clear use-case prioritization
Governance for shadow AI - unsanctioned use of AI tools by staff
Policy on AI vendor data handling (does your data train their models?)
Budget and plan for AI-driven productivity tools vs. one-off experiments
Cloud cost governance (FinOps) in place, not just cloud adoption
Disaster recovery and business continuity plans tested in last 12 months
Legacy system modernization roadmap with realistic timelines
SaaS sprawl inventory - ownership, access, and redundancy mapped
Data governance framework with clear ownership (not just IT's problem)
Master data quality standards defined for AI/analytics use
Data residency and sovereignty requirements mapped by jurisdiction
Digital literacy / AI literacy programs for the broader workforce
IT talent retention plan given competitive market for cloud/AI/security skills
Clear escalation path between IT, security, and business units
Technology stack decisions documented with rationale (avoid tool sprawl)
API-first / composable architecture to support fast integration and AI features
Technical debt tracked and budgeted for, not perpetually deferred
Scalability stress-tested against real growth projections
Clear framework for where AI is embedded in product vs. internal tooling
Model evaluation process - accuracy, bias, hallucination risk, cost per call
Versioning and rollback plan for AI features (models change/degrade over time)
IP and data provenance clarity for AI training data used in products
CI/CD pipeline maturity with automated security scanning built in (DevSecOps)
Code review and quality standards enforced, including for AI-generated code
Open-source dependency management - license compliance and vulnerability tracking
Engineering velocity metrics tied to actual business outcomes, not just output
R&D or innovation budget protected from short-term cuts
Build vs. buy vs. partner decisions revisited regularly (esp. AI vendors)
Engineering culture that attracts and retains scarce technical talent
Clear IP protection process for internally built tools and models
Cyber risk expressed in business terms (financial/operational impact) for the board
Risk register reviewed quarterly, tied to actual threat intelligence
Third-party/vendor risk management program - especially SaaS and AI vendors
Cyber insurance coverage reviewed against current risk profile
Ransomware playbook tested via tabletop exercise in last 6-12 months
AI-powered phishing/deepfake threats included in awareness training
Supply chain attack exposure mapped (SolarWinds/MOVEit-style scenarios)
Insider threat program in place, not just external-facing defenses
Security review process for AI tools before organizational adoption
Protections against prompt injection, data leakage, and model poisoning
Policy governing what data can/cannot be shared with third-party AI systems
Monitoring for AI agents with system access (emerging attack surface)
Mapping to current regulations: GDPR, DPDP Act (India), sector rules, EU AI Act etc.
Regular penetration testing and red-team exercises, not just automated scans
Incident response plan tested, with legal/PR/regulatory notification steps
Zero Trust architecture adoption status reviewed
MFA enforced everywhere, including privileged/admin accounts
Least-privilege access reviewed regularly, especially for departed employees
Credential exposure monitoring (dark web, leaked credential databases)
Network segmentation in place (flat networks are a major breach amplifier)
Redundant internet/WAN links for critical sites - no single point of failure
SD-WAN or equivalent for multi-site/remote-office performance
Bandwidth and latency monitoring tied to business-critical applications
Guest/IoT networks fully isolated from corporate systems
Hybrid/multi-cloud strategy documented - not accidental sprawl
Cloud resource tagging and cost allocation by department/project
Capacity planning reviewed quarterly against growth projections
Physical data center security audited (access logs, environmental controls)
Cloud provider SLAs matched against actual business uptime requirements
3-2-1 backup rule followed (3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite/immutable)
Backups tested via actual restore drills, not just completion logs
Immutable/air-gapped backups specifically to defend against ransomware
RTO/RPO targets defined per system and validated, not assumed
DR site or cloud failover tested at least annually with a real failover
Full asset inventory, including shadow IT devices and BYOD
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) deployed org-wide, not just servers
Patch management SLA enforced (critical patches within days, not months)
Mobile device management (MDM) for company and BYOD devices
End-of-life hardware/software tracked and replacement budgeted
Centralized identity provider (SSO) covering all major systems
Privileged access management (PAM) for admin/root accounts
Regular access recertification, especially after role changes or offboarding
Service accounts and API keys inventoried and rotated regularly
Unified monitoring across network, servers, cloud, and applications
SIEM in place with actual alert triage capacity
Automated alerting thresholds tuned to reduce noise/alert fatigue
Log retention aligned with compliance requirements
Auto-scaling configured for variable workloads
Load testing performed before major releases or expected traffic spikes
Database performance reviewed - indexing, query optimization
CDN usage for latency-sensitive, geographically distributed users
Infrastructure readiness for AI workloads (GPU/compute access, pipeline throughput)
Edge computing evaluated for latency-sensitive use cases (IoT, real-time analytics)
Green IT / energy efficiency metrics tracked
Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) adopted to reduce config drift and manual error
Unified AI governance policy - CIO (adoption), CTO (build), CISO (risk) all sign off
Joint incident response plan covering IT outage, security breach, and product failure
Shared vendor risk assessment process (no siloed procurement decisions)
Regular joint briefing to the board - one unified narrative
Budget alignment so security and resilience aren't first casualties of cost-cutting
Clear RACI matrix so ownership is obvious when something goes wrong
Business capability map maintained and linked to strategic objectives
